testing_centers.notes: Available at Pearson VUE test centers worldwide

id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. ID must match the name on the exam registration. Acceptable forms include passport, driver's license, or national ID card.
exam_rules: Open-book exam. Physical and electronic notes are permitted — building a comprehensive index is a key preparation strategy. No internet access during the exam except to pre-loaded approved materials. Proctored at Pearson VUE centers or online via ProctorU. Candidates have a 4-month window to schedule and take the exam after registration.
renewal_options: Certifications are valid for 4 years. Renewal requires 36 CPE (Continuing Professional Education) credits earned over the 4-year period, plus a $429 renewal fee. Alternatively, candidates may retake the current exam to renew.
target_audience: Incident handlers, incident handling team leads, system administrators, security practitioners, security architects, and any security personnel who are first responders
recommended_experience: Practical work experience in incident handling and computer security

prerequisites.description: Practical work experience in incident handling and computer security

retake_policy.notes: Two free practice tests are included with each exam registration. Candidates have a 4-month window to take the exam after registration. Retake fees apply after the first failed attempt. Contact GIAC for specific retake waiting periods.

objectives.title: Demonstrate a detailed understanding of how to conduct password attacks
Identify and defend against an attacker already in an environment, discover methods used to establish persistence, hide their presence, and achieve actions on objectives

domains.name: Detecting Exploitation and Covert Communications Tools

objectives.title: Demonstrate an understanding of how to identify and defend against the use of exploitation tools such as Metasploit and covert communications tools such as netcat
Demonstrate an understanding of how to identify and defend against endpoint specific attacks and pivoting in an environment
Demonstrate an understanding of common methods for exploiting insecure web application references
Demonstrate an understanding of the PICERL and DAIR incident handling processes and incident response challenges
Demonstrate an understanding of LLM prompt processing, risks, common attack methods, and defend against AI specific attacks in modern environments
Demonstrate an understanding of the steps necessary to perform basic malware analysis and understand how AI can be used to augment investigative efforts
Demonstrate an understanding of the steps necessary to perform effective investigations of network and log data
Demonstrate an understanding of how to discover and map networks and hosts, reveal services and vulnerabilities, and identify and defend against scanning

domains.name: Securing Credentials and Data in the Cloud

objectives.title: Demonstrate an understanding of how to identify, defend against, and mitigate password attacks and insecure storage in cloud-based environments
Demonstrate an understanding of SMB features, vulnerabilities, how to discover and access shares, and how to secure the service
Identify password hashes, understand password weaknesses, and secure passwords
Demonstrate the basics of interacting with and abusing access to web APIs
Demonstrate an understanding of common web application injection attacks
